subject: DPA: eSign logistics, breach notification timing & cross-border subprocessor notice
messages:
From: Julian Hayes <julian@fintechco.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@fintechco.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA redlines + notification timing request

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal completed a first pass on the standard Redwood DPA and attached our redlines (FinTechCo_DPA_Redlines_20270220.pdf). Two items they flagged as non-negotiable for our regulated payments work:

- Incident notification: must be "24 hours of confirmed knowledge" for any security breach affecting cardholder or PCI-relevant data.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days prior notice of new subprocessors and right to object for material changes.

Additionally we need to confirm the cross-border transfer mechanism for EU subjects — can Redwood execute SCC Annex with the DPA or do you require a separate flow?

Would prefer AdobeSign for our procurement signing (we have an existing SSO+audit flow there). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Attachments: FinTechCo_DPA_Redlines_20270220.pdf

Best,
Julian Hayes
Head of Payments, FinTechCo

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Julian Hayes <julian@fintechco.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + notification timing request

Julian —

Thanks for the redlines and for calling out the two hot spots. Looping in Neha (privacy counsel) and Marcus (Customer Success / onboarding) to weigh in on timing and eSign logistics. Quick thoughts:

- Notification window: we usually push for an initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware with a commitment to follow up as facts are confirmed. That said, for cardholder/PCI scoped exposures we understand the sensitivity and can propose an accelerated path — Neha, could you confirm if "24 hours of confirmed knowledge" is operationally feasible or whether we should propose a split timeline (e.g., 24h for confirmed exposures, 72h for suspected/under-investigation)?
- Subprocessor notice: our standard is 30 days for non-critical subprocessors and 72 hours for urgent security-impacting changes. We can map to your ask but need to keep some flexibility.
- SCCs / Cross-border: Redwood can include the SCC Annex as part of the DPA package. We typically bundle the SCC Annex v2 in the same eSign envelope to simplify execution.
- eSign platform: we use DocuSign by default (audit trail integrated into our procurement). We can accommodate AdobeSign vendor requests on a per-deal basis but need one of our legal team to be the envelope owner to maintain records.

I'll let Neha propose language and confirm our operational commitments. Marcus — please note the AdobeSign preference for procurement; can your onboarding team accept Adobe-signed DPAs into the contract system or do you need a DocuSign copy?

Thanks — I'll coordinate a short walkthrough if that helps expedite the redline closure.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Julian Hayes <julian@fintechco.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + notification timing request

Julian / team —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. I reviewed FinTechCo's version and drafted a compromise set of edits attached (Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20270219.pdf) that aim to:

1) Preserve operational feasibility — propose:
   - "Initial notification": Redwood will send an initial notification within 24 hours of confirmed knowledge where the breach materially impacts personal data or cardholder data; for incidents that are suspected or under active investigation, Redwood will provide an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and an interim update within 72 hours.
2) Subprocessor notice:
   - For non-security-impacting subprocessors, Redwood will provide 30 days' notice.
   - For security-impacting subprocessors (e.g., new cloud infra provider, data processing changes), Redwood will provide as much notice as practicable and, where possible, a 10-business-day notification; if immediate onboarding is required for security/availability reasons, Redwood will provide notice within 72 hours and include mitigation commitments.
3) SCCs: we can include SCC Annex v2 in the same envelope and attach signed Annexes to the DPA; we'll mark the Annex as executed when the primary signatory signs.

On eSign platform: we are okay with Redwood being the envelope owner even if FinTechCo uses AdobeSign on your side. If you can generate the Adobe envelope and invite our legal@redwood.com user as co-signer, our legal team will accept a match-back audit (we will require the same audit trail details). Practically, the path of least resistance is DocuSign with our envelope — we can provide the DocuSign envelope link and allow you to sign as a recipient using your Adobe credentials if needed.

I've attached the proposed language and highlighted the updated breach timeline text. If that looks good, Kimberly — can you confirm who at FinTechCo will be the signatory (procurement or legal)? Also, Marcus, please prepare the onboarding checklist for 72-hour emergency subprocessor notifications.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20270219.pdf, SCC_Annex_v2.docx

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Julian Hayes <julian@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 07:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + notification timing request

Neha / Kimberly —

Thanks for the thoughtful compromise language. A few follow-ups from our side:

- The 24h "confirmed knowledge" plus 24h acknowledgement/72h interim update approach is acceptable if the final clause states that "confirmed knowledge" means after reasonable internal verification of scope and affected data classes.
- For subprocessors, we can accept the tiered approach. Please add a short definition for "security-impacting" subprocessors so there is no ambiguity.
- AdobeSign: procurement insists on AdobeSign due to our SSO + archiving; however, legal is comfortable with your DocuSign audit artifact if Redwood joins as an envelope recipient and provides the DocuSign envelope ID and audit log after execution.

We are prepared to sign once (1) the final breach text includes the verification definition and (2) we receive the SCC Annex attached to the package.

Signatory will be: Sarah Connors, VP Procurement (sarah.connors@fintechco.com). Please send the eSign package to her.

Regards,
FinTechCo Legal

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@fintechco.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, DocuSign Support <support@docusign.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + notification timing request

Sarah / FinTechCo team —

Great — thanks for confirming signatory and the acceptance points. Plan of action: 

1) Neha will incorporate the definition of "confirmed knowledge" and the short definition for "security-impacting" subprocessors into the final redlines.
2) I will prepare a DocuSign envelope containing: Redwood_DPA_Redlines_20270219.pdf (final), SCC_Annex_v2.docx, and a signature page. Envelope owner will be kimberly_park@redwood.com; Sarah will be invited as primary recipient.
3) For audit and procurement compliance: once executed we will provide the DocuSign envelope ID and full audit log. If FinTechCo prefers to initiate via AdobeSign we can accept the Adobe envelope provided legal@redwood.com is included as a recipient; however, the path we plan will expedite execution.
4) Marcus will trigger the onboarding checklist contingent on executed DPA and will send a readout on subprocessor notice processes (timing, mailing list) within one business day of signing.

DocuSign draft envelope link (internal): https://app.docusign.com/envelope/status/ABC123456789 (will become active when sent).

Next steps for Sarah: please confirm which email address you want the envelope sent to (sarah.connors@fintechco.com is OK). If you require Adobe-only execution please let us know today and we will switch to co-sign mode; otherwise I will send the DocuSign envelope by EOD.

Thanks all — aiming to have this fully executed and onboarding-ready by the end of the week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
